title: Written Statement and Objections to Maintenance Application under Section 144 BNSS, 2023
whenToUse: Use when representing a husband or earning spouse defending against an inflated maintenance claim, establishing applicant's independent income, desertion, or concealment of assets.
variantComparisonNote: Formal defense written objection. Distinct from original maintenance petition.
youWillNeed: Income tax returns, bank statements, proof of applicant's qualifications and employment, proof of elderly dependent parents and medical liabilities.
legalBasis: Section 144(4) Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023; Rajnesh v. Neha (2020); Deb Narayan Halder v. Anushree Halder (2003).
mandatoryStatutoryIngredients: Specific denial of allegations of cruelty, harassment, or demand for dowry
Proof that applicant left matrimonial home voluntarily without justifiable cause
Establishment that applicant is professionally qualified or gainfully employed
Disclosure affidavit of assets and liabilities disclosing true financial obligations

particulars.label: Respondent (Husband)
particulars.description: Full legal name of respondent spouse

particulars.label: Applicant (Wife)
particulars.description: Full legal name of applicant spouse

aiBlocks.title: Preliminary Objections & Material Concealment
aiBlocks.draftingInstruction: Draft preliminary objections highlighting voluntary desertion under Section 144(4) BNSS, suppression of applicant's income and qualification, and misuse of summary proceedings.

aiBlocks.title: Para-Wise Rebuttal & Financial Realities
aiBlocks.draftingInstruction: Traverse each paragraph of the application, demonstrate respondent's genuine net income, statutory deductions, aged parent liabilities, and provide itemized rebuttal.

aiBlocks.title: Prayer for Dismissal / Rejection of Claim
aiBlocks.draftingInstruction: Draft formal prayer to dismiss the maintenance application with costs, or alternatively cap any nominal support strictly in accordance with Rajnesh v. Neha principles.
